Classroom reading-capacity evidence

Captured in Chromium against independent routed fixtures using Inter (heading 700, body 500). The left half of each comparison is before; the right half is after.

Fixture provenance: the lock/basketball visual is a crop reconstructed from the supplied screenshot because no original asset was available. It has no authored caption. The corrected visual baseline was recreated from the captured pre-change CSS geometry after removing the accidental caption; it is evidence reconstruction, not a pristine screenshot, and is not treated as proof of vertical-overflow improvement. The supplied screenshot appears teacher-adjusted toward a wider text pane; the automated reference comparisons preserve the product default rather than claiming a pixel-identical split.

Compatibility and limitations

  • Editor-preview and 1920×1080 PNG-export geometry are byte-for-byte equal to baseline: true.
  • Rich marks remained semantic and visible: Choose, highlighted does, underlined frustration.
  • Divider preference restored after 800×600 clamping; image-only/compact mode, font completion and actual browser fullscreen entry/exit converged and stopped creating probes.
  • At 800×600, the 240px rail minimum intentionally clamps the nominal ratio. At 390×844 adaptive landscape fitting is inactive and existing narrow responsive sizes apply.
  • The uncropped useful visual plus large timer/teacher control still produces vertical page flow at 1024×525 (after document height 574px). The corrected baseline is 570px, so no overflow-fix claim is made for this case.
  • Selected existing coverage passed for dense content, formula/mixed scripts, two visuals, 1000:00 timer, long footer, footer spacing invariance, no-rail/image-only modes, responsive export cleanliness, and short/reference compositions.

Generated evidence only; no production data was read or changed.
